sequence.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production hand-painted2D tactical RPG animation atlas matching supplied character EXACTLY. A mature bearded human warrior, chestnut short hair and neat beard, steel and bronze plate/chain armor, dark desaturated blue split tabard, brown gloves and sensible leather boots. Right hand holds a straight rigid one-handed sword, left arm carries a navy-and-bronze kite shield with a plain pale geometric motif. Identical shield sword and face throughout. Camera: orthographic shallow18-degree elevation, DIRECT BACK, entirely facing away, see back of hair and rear armor, no face or chest, same facing in ALL44cells. Maintain functional anatomical handedness; do not mirror weapon hands. Detailed painted brushwork/crisp material edges, warm muted light. Proportional anatomy, gloves, modest sensible boots. True clean transparency, no floor/shadow/text/labels/fringe. Large tall output2048x3840. EXACT4 COLUMNS x11 ROWS,44 separate fully visible figures, generous cell margins including weapons and lying body. SAME body size/head size in every row.
ROW1 four NEUTRAL IDLE breathing poses with relaxed upright straight legs, weapon safely lowered.
ROW2 four COMBAT IDLE breathing poses, weapon prepared forward at chest height.
ROWS3-4 EIGHT-frame natural NEUTRAL WALK loop, alternate left/right heel contact, loading, toe off, passing foot, normal modest stride, credible knee flexion.
ROWS5-6 EIGHT-frame natural COMBAT WALK loop, keep weapon in raised ready guard while feet alternate; never revert to weapon dangling at thigh.
ROWS7-8 EIGHT-frame ATTACK: one sword cut behind kite shield: front guard sword pointing UP not down, hip/shoulder backswing, left shield braces forward, step, right-handed diagonal cut, follow-through, recover, guard. Sword in anatomical RIGHT hand, shield on anatomical LEFT forearm irrespective of facing.
ROW9 FOUR HIT frames: shoulder struck, recoil, stabilize feet, return guard.
ROWS10-11 EIGHT DEATH/FALL frames: struck, torso buckles, knees bend, knee ground, hand floor, body falls onto side, lands, final full body lying still. No gore. Articulated fall not rigid upright rotation. Fixed camera and facing, full silhouettes. Rows are chronological left to right; no omitted cells. Every sword/shaft remains straight and SAME physical length.

sequence_shield_inside.prompt: Precise sprite-sheet correction for an existing painted tactical RPG. sequence_rear_stance.prompt:
Edit the provided painted tactical RPG sprite sheet. The edit target is the FIRST reference, a transparent 4-column by 11-row sheet with exactly 44 separate full-body frames of the SAME brown-haired, blue-and-gold armored sword-and-shield warrior facing EXACTLY AWAY from the camera (north, shallow tactical camera). The second reference is the current native combat idle for identity/detail. Keep his identity, painterly detail, exposure, material colors, body height, proportional boots, shield on anatomical LEFT, one-handed sword in anatomical RIGHT hand, and EXACT frame chronology/layout. Do not turn his head or torso toward camera and do not show a face.
Only requested corrections: (1) in planted standing poses give him a comfortable shoulder-width base with feet distinctly apart, like the other accepted warriors: increase separation between boot centers by about 40 percent, keep legs naturally straight, knees relaxed, boots same modest size. No bow legs or exaggerated split. Apply coherent weight shifts to attack/hit, while walk rows keep real alternating steps rather than a wide static slide. (2) the held sword must be IN FRONT OF HIS TORSO, away from camera, substantially hidden by his back/torso/right upper arm in exact rear view. Move the right hand/forearm toward the front of his midline, foreshorten the blade into depth; show only naturally unoccluded portions, e.g. a short tip beside or above the shoulder in ready stance. Do NOT draw the whole long sword sticking diagonally far out to the right in neutral/ready/walk poses. Do NOT shrink/bend/remove the sword: it is still rigid and full length but occluded by the body. During the actual attack sweep the blade can become visible naturally. Preserve the plain brown wood/leather INNER shield face, straps, hand grip and forearm attachment; no exterior emblem on this rear face.
Rows 1-2: four neutral idle and four ready/combat idle frames with the new planted wider stance and subtle upper-body breathing. Rows 3-4: eight sequential neutral walk frames, alternating foot contacts. Rows 5-6: eight sequential combat walk frames, alternating foot contacts, sword mostly occluded in front of body. Rows 7-8: eight sequential one-handed sword attack frames, anticipation, forward cut, follow-through, recovery, stable broad base; blade rigid. Row 9: four hit/recoil frames maintaining equipment and rear view. Rows 10-11: eight death/fall frames: preserve these original poses and anatomy as closely as possible, do not redesign them. All44 full figures separated, ordered left-to-right then top-to-bottom, generous clear alpha gaps, nothing clipped, no text, no extra weapons, no floor, no shadows, no background, actual transparent alpha. This is a narrow correction to the existing painted character, not a new character or a different art style.
